preset_name: VHS Restoration - Stage 1: Artifact Stripping (Iris LQ)
description: First pass: Clean up VHS artifacts, ringing, and noise at native resolution. Do NOT upscale yet.
use_case: 1990s analog VHS tapes, Video8, Hi8, DV camcorder footage

preprocessing.method_topaz: Enable 'Interlaced' input mode, set Field Order carefully (BFF or TFF), use 2x Deinterlace (Bob)
preprocessing.note: Never feed interlaced VHS directly into Topaz. Deinterlace first.

revert_compression.tooltip: Strip DCT blocks from old tape encoding.

improve_detail.tooltip: Minimal—VHS has low native detail. Over-improving causes artifacts.

sharpen.tooltip: Keep at 0. Never sharpen in Pass 1.

reduce_noise.tooltip: Aggressive noise reduction. VHS is very noisy.

dehalo.tooltip: CRITICAL. VHS has heavy analog edge enhancement halos. Iris LQ is tuned for this.

anti_alias_deblur.tooltip: Positive = deblur. Counter VHS softness and interlacing blur.

recover_original_detail.tooltip: Low blend—mostly AI cleaning in Stage 1.

why_iris_lq: Iris LQ is specifically trained on low-resolution interlaced video. Proteus would hallucinate plastic skin. Iris strips noise uniformly without adding texture.
expected_output_stage_1: 720x480 (NTSC) or 720x576 (PAL), deinterlaced to 59.94fps or 50fps, cleaned of VHS artifacts but still low-res
next_step: Export this Stage 1 output, then feed into Stage 2 (Proteus v4 upscaling)
common_mistakes: Upscaling directly from interlaced VHS to 4K (causes ghosting + hallucinations)
Using Proteus or Nyx in Stage 1 (designed for higher quality input)
Setting Dehalo below 40 (VHS ringing won't be removed)
Trying to recover detail (VHS has none; just clean what exists)
